miltank_milk.problem: Pixelmon 9.2.3 MiltankInteraction.processInteract shrinks the held minecraft:bucket and puts a new minecraft:milk_bucket into the selected slot (last bucket) or adds it to the inventory; Society's milkBan.js then zeroes every vanilla milk bucket and gives an empty bucket back.
design: ItemEvents.entityInteracted registered for minecraft:bucket: when the hand is MAIN_HAND, the target type is pixelmon:pixelmon, the bucket is not on cooldown, target.getSpecies().getName() is Miltank and target.getNumInteractions() > 0, the player's uuid is remembered with the level game time. These are the conditions under which Pixelmon produces the bucket in the same call (PixelmonEntity.mobInteract returns early for a cooling item, AbstractInteractionsEntity.mobInteract needs the main hand, an interaction object and numInteractions > 0, MiltankInteraction needs Items.BUCKET).

PlayerEvents.inventoryChanged registered for minecraft:milk_bucket: a remembered interaction not older than 2 game ticks is used up; the first vanilla milk bucket in player.inventory.items loses one item; the player is given 1 society:milk and 1 minecraft:bucket. Without a remembered interaction the handler returns at once.

After the two items were given: when no other vanilla milk bucket is left and the event carries a menu slot (slot >= 0), the stack passed with the event is emptied as well. A stack reported with slot -1 is never emptied.
proof_from_bytes: Handler order: dev.latvian.mods.kubejs.event.EventHandler.post runs the containers registered for the event's extra id (extraEventContainers.get(extraId)) before the generic eventContainers. PlayerEvents.INVENTORY_CHANGED and ItemEvents.ENTITY_INTERACTED both carry ItemEvents.SUPPORTS_ITEM, and KubeJSInventoryListener.slotChanged posts with stack.getItem() as extra id. milkBan.js registers without an id, so the overlay handler always runs first, whatever the file load order (which is file-system order for equal priorities: the fixed-final log does not load scripts alphabetically).

What milkBan.js sees: AbstractContainerMenu.broadcastChanges builds one memoized copy per slot (Suppliers.memoize(itemstack::copy)); triggerSlotListeners stores that copy in lastSlots and passes it to the listeners; synchronizeSlotToRemote sends the same copy to the client. InventoryChangedEventJS.getItem returns that copy. ItemStack.getItem returns Items.AIR when count <= 0, and ItemStackKJS.kjs$getId is getItem().kjs$getId(), so after the overlay empties the copy milkBan.js reads e.item.id as minecraft:air, fails its bannedItems check and returns before the chat line. The slot itself was emptied by the overlay, so menu state, client and inventory agree.

If milkBan.js does run (another vanilla milk bucket is present, or society:milk is missing) it loops over player.inventory.items and only touches stacks whose id equals the banned id; the exchanged stack has count 0 and id minecraft:air.

An exception inside a handler ends the handler chain of that event (EventHandlerContainer.handle throws EventExit and post skips the remaining containers), so both handler bodies are wrapped; on failure nothing is remembered or exchanged and Society's handlers run as before.

Timing: PacketUtils.ensureRunningOnSameThread queues the interaction packet as a task of the server thread, so it runs outside ServerLevel.tick; ServerLevel.tick calls tickTime() before it ticks entities, and ServerPlayer.tick calls containerMenu.broadcastChanges() every tick. The bucket is therefore reported one game tick after the remembered time (never more); the window of 2 leaves one tick of slack. KubeJS exposes Level.getGameTime as getTime (LevelMixin @RemapForJS).

Script access to Pixelmon objects: ScriptManager.visibleToScripts only filters ClassShutter.TYPE_CLASS_IN_PACKAGE (2), i.e. Java.loadClass; members of objects handed to a script are reachable. PixelmonEntity is public; getSpecies() (AbstractBaseEntity), Species.getName() and getNumInteractions() (AbstractInteractionsEntity) are public.
Pixelmon absent: the file has the KubeJS property "requires: pixelmon" (ScriptFileInfo.skipLoading -> Platform.isModLoaded) and is not loaded at all.

Second source of the event: KubeJSItemEventHandler.crafted and .smelted also post PlayerEvents.INVENTORY_CHANGED, with the real crafted or smelted stack and slot -1 (not a menu copy). The script therefore empties event.item only when event.slot >= 0, the value KubeJSInventoryListener.slotChanged passes (the menu slot index); with slot -1 the exchange itself still runs on player.inventory.items and the passed stack is left untouched, so Society's handler prints its line and finds nothing to confiscate.
miltank_milk.never_affects_other_milk: A vanilla milk bucket is exchanged only while a remembered Miltank interaction of the same player is at most 2 game ticks old, and each one pays for one bucket. Residual case: the remembered interaction is cancelled by another mod after the script saw it (so Pixelmon gives nothing) and an unrelated vanilla milk bucket reaches the same player within those 2 ticks; that bucket would become society:milk plus a bucket instead of a bucket.
miltank_milk.rhino_scenarios: harness/scenario_miltank.js with Society's real milkBan.js, both load orders, identical results: single bucket, repeat by the same player, stack of three buckets, foreign milk without interaction, other Pokemon, Miltank without milkings, off hand, bucket on cooldown, cow, expired interaction, Miltank milk plus foreign milk in one tick, missing Pixelmon methods, missing society:milk, full inventory. harness/scenario_miltank_java.js repeats them with Java objects behind every value the scripts touch (Fakes.java: bean getters, a Java list of stacks, enum hand, java.util.UUID, long game time), so the property access, list iteration, string comparison and arithmetic of both scripts run through Rhino's Java interop.
runtime_probe: A wild Miltank cannot be milked in Pixelmon 9.2.3: PixelmonInteraction.getInteraction is only called from AbstractInteractionsEntity.onSendout, and onSendout is only referenced by PokeBallEntity, OccupiedPokeBallEntity and ExecuteActionGoal. Use a Miltank owned by the player and sent out of its ball (for example give one with Pixelmon's /pokegive, then send it out); for a Miltank that was never milked the first milking becomes available on the first tick after send-out, the second after 800 to 1399 more ticks (PixelmonInteraction.resetCounter).

Hold exactly one minecraft:bucket in the main hand and right-click the Miltank: expect 1 society:milk and 1 minecraft:bucket in the inventory, no minecraft:milk_bucket, and no "need milk pail" chat line.
Hold a stack of several buckets and repeat when a milking is available: expect the stack unchanged in total (one bucket taken, one given back) plus 1 society:milk.
Control: /give <player> minecraft:milk_bucket must still be turned into an empty bucket with Society's "need milk pail" chat line.
Control: right-click a Miltank with no milking left (third try within a minute) and a non-Miltank Pokemon with a bucket: nothing is given and nothing is printed.
limits: With a full inventory Pixelmon drops the milk bucket at the player's feet (DropItemHelper.giveItemStack); picked up later it is outside the 2 tick window and Society's rule turns it into an empty bucket, as before this overlay.
milkBan.js and this script look at player.inventory.items (the 36 main slots) only; Pixelmon never places the bucket elsewhere.
The script gives plain society:milk (the small cow milk of Society's husbandryDefinitions.js, cowMilk.sm) without quality data.

api_facts_from_bytes: RecipesEventJS.remove(IDFilter) marks originalRecipes.get(id) as removed; remove, replaceInput and countRecipes only ever see originalRecipes, never script-added recipes.
RecipesEventJS.countRecipes(RecipeFilter) returns an int; a filter object with id and input becomes AndFilter(IDFilter, InputFilter) (RecipeFilter.of).

RecipesEventJS.shaped is kubejs:shaped (common.properties serverOnly=false); ShapedRecipeJS.getSerializationTypeFunction writes minecraft:crafting_shaped when no kubejs: flag is set. RecipeJS.id(ResourceLocation) only sets the id.

RecipeJS.replaceInput replaces every input component the match overlaps (ItemComponents.INPUT.isInput -> IngredientMatch.contains -> Ingredient.test); only changed components are written back into the original JSON, so pattern, result, count and id stay.

IngredientKJS.kjs$subtract (exposed as subtract through @RemapPrefixForJS) -> IngredientForgeHelper.subtract -> net.minecraftforge.common.crafting.DifferenceIngredient.of(base, subtracted); its toJson writes {"type":"forge:difference","base":...,"subtracted":...}, test() is base.test && !subtracted.test, and DifferenceIngredientMixin keeps it usable for KubeJS input matching.

Type wrappers registered by BuiltinKubeJSPlugin: RecipeFilter, ReplacementMatch, InputReplacement, Ingredient, InputItem, OutputItem, ItemStack, Item, ResourceLocation; NativeJavaObject.coerceTypeImpl applies the wrapper of the parameter type to the unwrapped argument, also when the argument is a Java object.

ScriptFileInfo.preload: a line starting with // that matches ^(\w+)\s*[:=]?\s*(-?\w+)$ is a file property; priority, requires, ignored, ignore and packmode are read. ScriptFile.compareTo sorts by descending priority (stable), so priority -100 loads after every priority 0 file.

No recipe of the staged profile uses forge:difference yet. recipeessentials 4.0 (the RecipeManager in use according to the sweep verifier's reading of debug.log) keys its cache on the grid contents and calls Recipe.matches on the candidates; it does not look inside ingredients.
corrections_to_sweep_claims: Verifier, miltank-milk fix assessment: "milkBan.js will still print the need-milk-pail line unless that file is edited" does not hold. The event carries the menu's copy of the stack; emptying it makes milkBan.js return on its first line. No Society file is edited and no line is printed.

Verifier, same assessment: a "// priority:" header to load before milkBan.js is not needed and would not be the mechanism; handlers registered with an item id run before handlers registered without one.

Auditor, pokeball-base-recipe-collisions: the scanner skipped forge:conditional recipes and applied Society removals first. Re-scanned without those filters: cluttered:small_shelf and cluttered:small_shelf_pink also share the wooden base grid, but Society removes both recipes, so the proven pair list (trapdoor, item shelf, present/box, four Botania slabs, crafty crate, Oreganized silver block) is complete for crafting recipes found in JARs, kubejs/data and Society scripts.

Task text, item 4: the Botania ingredients are wood blocks (botania:livingwood, botania:dreamwood and the stripped forms), not logs, as the verifier already noted; exactly these four ids and botania:dreamwood_planks are excluded.

limits: The scripts were not run in the game. The script logic ran in the pack's Rhino build against stand-ins; the Java side (type wrappers, recipe JSON round trip of forge:difference, client sync, JEI/EMI display) is proven from decompiled bytes only.
The static scan cannot see run-time generated recipes (see collision_scan.not_covered).

All hashes under inputs are the versions these facts were read from; a different Pixelmon, Whimsy Deco, Supplementaries, Botania, Oreganized, KubeJS or Rhino build needs a new scan before the scripts are installed.

reviewer_changes.change: (1) event.item is emptied only when event.slot >= 0: KubeJS posts PlayerEvents.inventoryChanged from its crafted and smelted hooks with the real result stack and slot -1, and emptying that stack would delete an item. (2) The two player.give calls now run before the copy is emptied, so nothing after the bucket was taken can prevent the hand-out. (3) Two comment lines describe (1).
